correctness.rationale: For beta>=2, the periodic Gaussian has strictly negative derivative on (0,1/2) from an exact Jacobi triple product; each paired real-part correction is nonnegative because u exp(-beta u^2) decreases for u>=1/2. The only boundary zeros are the parity-forced ones, with the x=0 sine-series first harmonic dominating all higher terms by a rigorously summed geometric-moment bound <1. Reflection excludes x>1/2. Fourier-transform Zak duality has a nonzero factor and maps beta<2 to beta'>2, permuting the listed three zeros. All endpoints and quantifiers are included. Supplementary diagnostic script checks exact transform identity at finite inputs; no finite sample is used as proof.

originality.rationale: Faulhuber (arXiv:2502.09510, first posted 2025-02-13, Section 4 Conjecture 4.1) expressly conjectures three Zak zeros for all generalized first-Hermite windows with arbitrary dilation and chirp, and leaves the exclusion of additional zeros open. The new analytic argument proves the arbitrary-dilation no-chirp subcase, not claimed in the inspected primary section. published-finding corpus searches of precise zero-set statements and analogous global scaling results did not find stronger coverage. The absence of an indexed duplicate is not proof of novelty; earlier older results remain a risk.

value.rationale: All-scale exact nonexistence of extra zeros addresses an explicit recent first-Hermite Zak-zero conjecture in its nonchirped arbitrary-dilation subfamily; these zeros govern obstructions for periodic Gabor sampling.
